visual_anchor: Territorial diffusion restriction, early CT ischemic changes, and arterial occlusion on CTA.
rationale: Core emergency with management relevant imaging.

visual_anchor: Blood in basal cisterns and sulci on CT, with a causative aneurysm on CTA or angiography.
rationale: Distinct hemorrhagic emergency from intraparenchymal hemorrhage.

visual_anchor: Rim enhancing epidural collection with cord or cauda equina compression on MRI.
rationale: Distinct imageable spinal infection requiring urgent recognition.

visual_anchor: Anterior cord diffusion restriction; sagittal pencil like signal and axial owl eyes may occur.
rationale: Named vascular cord disease; signs are supportive rather than uniquely diagnostic.

visual_anchor: MRI demonstrates the compressive cause; clinical saddle sensory and sphincter findings define the emergency.
rationale: Add emergency presentation and red flags to lumbar disc herniation and stenosis pages, with cross links to tumors and infection.

visual_anchor: Facial diplegia or flaccid weakness; smooth cauda equina root enhancement can support an atypical case.
rationale: Core clinical syndrome; enhancement is nonspecific and MRI is not a routine confirmatory test.

visual_anchor: Symmetric central pontine signal with peripheral sparing, sometimes with extrapontine lesions.
rationale: Recognizable toxic metabolic MRI pattern.

visual_anchor: Bilateral globus pallidus injury and delayed white matter abnormalities may appear on MRI.
rationale: Important toxic exposure with a memorable imaging differential; normal early imaging does not exclude it.

visual_anchor: Susceptibility blooming coating cerebellar folia, brainstem, and cranial nerves.
rationale: Distinct distribution and chronic clinical syndrome; separate from cortical siderosis in cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

visual_anchor: Alternating concentric rings on T2 and diffusion imaging.
rationale: Distinctive concentric demyelinating lesion pattern; overlap with multiple sclerosis does not mean every case is established MS.

visual_anchor: Numerous punctate and curvilinear enhancing foci centered on the pons and cerebellar peduncles.
rationale: Recognizable inflammatory syndrome; label as a diagnosis requiring exclusion of mimics, especially lymphoma.

visual_anchor: Corpus callosum swelling or injury with selective central layer involvement.
rationale: Distinct alcohol or malnutrition associated callosal disease.

visual_anchor: Symmetric dentate nucleus abnormalities, sometimes involving the splenium or brainstem.
rationale: Characteristic medication associated imaging pattern.

visual_anchor: Curvilinear DWI hyperintensity along the corticomedullary junction.
rationale: Strong imaging clue beyond the confirmatory skin biopsy; not present in every case.

canonical_name: Biotin thiamine responsive basal ganglia disease
visual_anchor: Symmetric caudate and putamen swelling or injury on MRI in acute encephalopathy.
rationale: Treatable metabolic disorder with an important imaging trigger; genetic confirmation is needed.

canonical_name: HTRA1 related cerebral small vessel disease
visual_anchor: Leukoencephalopathy with lacunes; classic CARASIL adds early alopecia and spondylosis, and an arc sign can involve the pons and middle cerebellar peduncles.
rationale: Distinct from CADASIL; use HTRA1 spectrum title and CARASIL as a searchable phenotype.

visual_anchor: Bilateral thalamic lesions, sometimes involving basal ganglia and brainstem.
rationale: Imageable neuroinfection; pattern requires epidemiologic and laboratory context.

visual_anchor: Brainstem and cerebellar peduncle inflammation or microabscesses on MRI.
rationale: Distinctive hindbrain distribution makes a useful neuroinfection topic.

visual_anchor: Longitudinal gray matter predominant spinal cord T2 signal with acute asymmetric flaccid weakness.
rationale: Important pediatric syndrome distinct from poliomyelitis.

visual_anchor: Progressive white matter abnormalities and atrophy are nonspecific; EEG and virologic evidence establish the syndrome.
rationale: A distinct delayed measles associated CNS disease, not an acute measles subtype; proposed MRI is nonspecific and key EEG or serologic findings are outside the clinical and radiologic image focus. Cross link from measles if expanded later.

visual_anchor: Bilateral pallidal signal abnormalities, with chronic T2 changes; early bilirubin injury can be T1 bright.
rationale: Core neonatal toxic brain injury; state sequence and disease stage correctly.

canonical_name: Germinal matrix and intraventricular hemorrhage of prematurity
visual_anchor: Caudothalamic groove hemorrhage and intraventricular blood on cranial ultrasound.
rationale: Distinct neonatal hemorrhage pattern; include periventricular hemorrhagic infarction as an associated venous injury.

visual_anchor: Periventricular cysts or white matter volume loss with irregular ventricular margins.
rationale: Classic injury of prematurity, distinct from term neonatal hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy.

visual_anchor: Excess small gyri with an irregular cortical surface and gray white junction on MRI.
rationale: Imaging defined cortical malformation; keep regional forms together.

visual_anchor: Gray matter signal nodules lining the lateral ventricles.
rationale: Distinct migration disorder from subcortical band heterotopia.

visual_anchor: Intraventricular or spinal mass; posterior fossa tumors may extend through the fourth ventricular outlets.
rationale: Major missing neurooncology topic; organize by current molecular and anatomic classification, not an assertion that every type is the same tumor.

visual_anchor: Cortical or subcortical infiltrative mass often containing calcification.
rationale: Important brain tumor differential; imaging cannot establish IDH mutation or 1p19q codeletion.

visual_anchor: Superficial cortical tumor, often temporal, sometimes cystic with a mural nodule or calcification.
rationale: Distinct epilepsy associated glioneuronal tumor; separate from DNET.

visual_anchor: Bubbly multinodular cortical lesion with little mass effect in a patient with epilepsy.
rationale: Separate tumor with a useful MRI pattern; do not combine with ganglioglioma.

visual_anchor: Scapular winging with patchy muscle denervation edema or atrophy on MRI.
rationale: Recognizable clinical and imaging syndrome, distinct from entrapment neuropathy.

visual_anchor: Frontal and anterior temporal predominant atrophy or hypometabolism.
rationale: Major dementia syndrome with imageable regional patterns; keep phenotypes within one topic.

visual_anchor: Symmetric cerebellar and posterior cerebral white matter abnormalities.
rationale: Characteristic exposure related distribution; preserve common chasing the dragon search term.

visual_anchor: Symmetric dorsal column cord signal may mimic vitamin B12 related subacute combined degeneration.
rationale: Teach as an etiologic differential in the existing dorsal column syndrome page; no independent visual discriminator is supplied.

visual_anchor: Dorsal column inverted V signal from functional vitamin B12 inactivation.
rationale: Add exposure specific cause and clinical teaching to existing subacute combined degeneration.

visual_anchor: Confluent white matter injury, callosal thinning, persistent diffusion abnormalities, and small CT calcifications.
rationale: Distinct adult white matter disorder; use current spectrum name and retain ALSP as a search alias.

visual_anchor: Cystic bone lesions paired with frontal predominant white matter degeneration.
rationale: Distinct combined skeletal and neurologic syndrome.

canonical_name: Retinal vasculopathy with cerebral leukoencephalopathy and systemic manifestations
visual_anchor: Retinal vascular abnormalities and enhancing white matter lesions that can resemble tumors.
rationale: Multisystem TREX1 associated syndrome; separate from Aicardi Goutieres syndrome.

visual_anchor: Iron sensitive substantia nigra and pallidal signal, with a T1 bright nigral halo in later disease.
rationale: Distinct NBIA phenotype with strong MRI teaching value.

visual_anchor: Posterior cortical and thalamic MRI abnormalities with refractory epilepsy and liver disease.
rationale: Recognizable POLG related clinicoradiologic phenotype; findings are not specific alone.

visual_anchor: Symmetric thalamic lesions, sometimes with concentric hemorrhagic or necrotic components.
rationale: Distinct infection triggered encephalopathy rather than infectious encephalitis itself.

visual_anchor: Deep gray, brainstem, or anterior horn abnormalities can accompany encephalitis or acute flaccid paralysis.
rationale: Useful neuroinfectious differential; MRI may be normal and laboratory confirmation is essential.

visual_anchor: Dorsal brainstem signal with a compatible hand foot and mouth eruption.
rationale: Distinct neuroinvasive syndrome with a recognizable posterior brainstem pattern; cross link to hand foot and mouth disease rather than equating the two.

visual_anchor: Diffuse edema and meningeal enhancement lack a reliable distinguishing imaging pattern.
rationale: The proposal relies on organism microscopy and late nonspecific necrosis, insufficient for the current clinical and radiologic scope.

visual_anchor: Focal or diffuse thickened enhancing dura on MRI.
rationale: Thickened enhancing dura is nonspecific, and the idiopathic label is exclusionary. Prioritize etiology defined or more distinctive clinicoradiologic topics.

visual_anchor: Radial perivascular enhancement extending from the ventricles, with possible cord or meningeal involvement.
rationale: Distinct autoimmune syndrome from genetic GFAP associated Alexander disease; imaging is supportive.

visual_anchor: Multifocal infarct like lesions of different ages or other variable brain MRI abnormalities.
rationale: Existing Hematology topic already names the same disease; expand neurologic coverage.

visual_anchor: Cerebral hemiatrophy with ipsilateral calvarial thickening and sinus enlargement.
rationale: Coherent clinicoradiologic syndrome with a memorable structural pattern.

visual_anchor: Porencephaly, small vessel disease, and variable ocular abnormalities such as cataract.
rationale: Distinct genetic multisystem disease spectrum; avoid separate pages for every manifestation.

visual_anchor: Near absence of cerebral hemispheres replaced by fluid, with preserved falx and variable deep structures.
rationale: Distinct severe malformation from hydrocephalus and holoprosencephaly.

canonical_name: Horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis
visual_anchor: Split pons and butterfly shaped medulla with progressive scoliosis.
rationale: Distinct structural brainstem and skeletal syndrome.

visual_anchor: Fusion of cerebellar hemispheres across a deficient vermis.
rationale: Imaging defined hindbrain malformation; syndromic associations belong within the topic.

visual_anchor: Small ventral pons and cerebellum; a dragonfly configuration occurs in some forms.
rationale: Use a single clinicoradiologic family topic with genetic subtypes; no claim that the dragonfly pattern occurs in all forms.

visual_anchor: Congenital weakness or contractures with extensive characteristic white matter signal abnormalities.
rationale: Distinct muscle and brain phenotype, not covered by Walker Warburg or Ullrich disease.

visual_anchor: Focal ventral cord displacement and kinking through a dural defect on MRI.
rationale: Distinct structural cause of progressive myelopathy.

visual_anchor: Focal dorsal cord indentation producing a sagittal scalpel sign, sometimes with a syrinx.
rationale: Specific structural lesion; distinguish from ventral cord herniation and arachnoid cyst.

visual_anchor: Extra axial CSF like lesion with marked DWI hyperintensity.
rationale: Distinct intracranial developmental lesion from cutaneous epidermal inclusion cyst.

visual_anchor: Fat containing intracranial lesion, with disseminated fat droplets after rupture.
rationale: Distinct developmental lesion with a strong CT and MRI anchor.

visual_anchor: Bubbly intraventricular mass near the foramen of Monro and septum pellucidum.
rationale: Useful age and location based tumor pattern.

visual_anchor: Lobulated avidly enhancing intraventricular frond like mass with hydrocephalus.
rationale: Distinct ventricular tumor from ependymoma; imaging alone does not establish benignity.

visual_anchor: Superficial hemispheric cyst and mural nodule, sometimes with meningeal contact.
rationale: Named cortical tumor with useful age, epilepsy, and location context.

visual_anchor: Thin corpus callosum and ears of the lynx white matter signal near the frontal horns.
rationale: Distinct MRI supported spastic paraplegia; sign also occurs in SPG15 and is not uniquely diagnostic.

visual_anchor: Calf pseudohypertrophy and muscle fatty replacement overlap Duchenne disease.
rationale: Broaden existing Duchenne page to dystrophinopathies and show Becker comparison; a separate near identical visual page adds little.

visual_anchor: Miyoshi phenotype shows prominent posterior calf wasting, with selective muscle involvement on imaging.
rationale: Use a single DYSF spectrum topic including Miyoshi and limb girdle presentations.

visual_anchor: Long myopathic face, ptosis, ophthalmoparesis, and severe neonatal hypotonia.
rationale: Visible phenotype supports a clinical atlas entry beyond its biopsy finding.

visual_anchor: Hypotonia is nonspecific; central cores are a muscle histology finding.
rationale: No sufficiently distinctive clinical or radiologic anchor is supplied.

canonical_name: Hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies
visual_anchor: Recurrent focal palsies have no stable distinctive photograph; tomacula require nerve histology.
rationale: Primarily electrodiagnostic and genetic diagnosis with weak standalone visual value.

visual_anchor: Asymmetric hand wasting and nerve enlargement are nonspecific.
rationale: Prioritize stronger phenotype and image based additions; diagnosis depends on electrophysiology and clinical context.

visual_anchor: PAS positive sweat gland inclusions are histologic.
rationale: The proposed teaching image is pathology rather than a clinical or radiologic manifestation.

visual_anchor: Ragged red fibers are histologic and multiple lipomas are variable and nonspecific.
rationale: Insufficient independent clinical or radiologic anchor for current release.

visual_anchor: Cerebellar atrophy alone is nonspecific; pallidal iron may appear later.
rationale: Defer the proposed infantile phenotype until a distinct reproducible clinical and MRI image set is demonstrated.

visual_anchor: Smooth tongue from absent fungiform papillae and absent overflow emotional tears.
rationale: Directly photographable diagnostic phenotype distinct from congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis.

visual_anchor: Central interphalangeal erosions with gull wing or saw tooth configuration.
rationale: Add an erosive phenotype section to existing osteoarthritis; new imaging content does not require a new disease page.

visual_anchor: Digital clubbing with symmetric long bone periostosis and parallel cortical scintigraphic uptake.
rationale: Useful acquired syndrome across multiple causes; distinct from primary pachydermoperiostosis.

visual_anchor: Joint fragmentation, debris, disorganization, and collapse; rocker bottom foot in advanced midfoot disease.
rationale: Coherent image defined syndrome across etiologies; keep all joints and causes together.

visual_anchor: Diffuse femoral head and neck marrow edema, later osteopenia, without the typical focal necrotic boundary.
rationale: Important clinical and imaging differential from osteonecrosis and insufficiency fracture.

visual_anchor: Periarticular bone cysts and destructive spondyloarthropathy after long term dialysis.
rationale: Distinct precursor protein and distribution from systemic AL amyloidosis.

visual_anchor: Rapidly progressive woody palmar thickening with flexion contractures and polyarthritis.
rationale: Distinct photographable paraneoplastic syndrome; retain underlying malignancy associations in the page.

visual_anchor: Painless lateral proximal interphalangeal soft tissue thickening without erosions.
rationale: Useful visible mimic of inflammatory arthritis.

canonical_name: Camptodactyly arthropathy coxa vara pericarditis syndrome
visual_anchor: Camptodactyly, noninflammatory joint swelling, and coxa vara with short femoral necks.
rationale: Distinct PRG4 associated clinical and skeletal phenotype.

visual_anchor: Carpal and tarsal osteolysis with palmoplantar nodules and contractures.
rationale: Canonical MMP2 related MONA topic; Torg and NAO belong here, while MMP14 Winchester syndrome is separate.

visual_anchor: Progressive osteolysis and contractures overlap MONA.
rationale: Keep separate in disease ontology; defer a second closely overlapping visual page until its own useful clinical and imaging set is demonstrated.

visual_anchor: Childhood diffuse lung disease with ground glass, cysts, and nodules paired with arthritis.
rationale: Distinct inherited immune dysregulation syndrome; place in Immunology with rheumatology and pulmonology cross links.

visual_anchor: Early aortic or valve calcification, abnormal dentition, and acro osteolysis.
rationale: Strong multisystem radiographic phenotype.

visual_anchor: Indurated bound down skin with hypertrichosis and joint contractures.
rationale: Directly visible fibrosing disorder distinct from stiff person syndrome and systemic sclerosis.

visual_anchor: Periarticular cutaneous nodules with rapidly developing flexion contractures.
rationale: Recognizable clinicocutaneous syndrome; biopsy supports diagnosis.

visual_anchor: Irregular bulky periosteal new bone, often involving ribs, clavicles, or scapulae.
rationale: Distinct medication associated radiographic phenotype from smoother secondary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.
